views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Go into the G20 Osaka meeting with China seeking a truce that restarts negotiations while holding off on the threatened $300 billion consumer-goods tariff tranche. Keep the existing $250B tariffs and enforcement demands as leverage, but do not escalate into the next round, which would hit US consumers, retailers and the holiday season directly. Make the summit a genuine de-escalation off-ramp.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderate-to-high, not existential, because the US economy is still holding (Q1 GDP ~3.1%, Michigan sentiment 98.2, industrial production roughly flat, CPI mild) even as the trade war drags global growth (IMF global GDP hit, World Bank's slowest trade growth in a decade, per June 10 NYT). But the danger is real and rising: the market is already flashing warning — the 10-year yield collapsed from ~2.5% in April to 2.05% by June 26 and the 2-year to 1.77%, with Baa spreads loosening, i.e. rate markets pricing in aggressive Fed cuts on growth fear. Escalating to the $300B tranche would be a 'regressive tax' on households (~$831/year per NY Fed, 2M jobs per Business Roundtable study; 'catastrophic' per Nike/Adidas; 600+ companies' letter) at the exact point retailers are placing holiday orders. China has already retaliated against US agriculture (soybeans on the $60B/$110B list, prompting a ~$16B farm bailout) and signaled rare-earth and 'unreliable entity list' leverage. None of this is yet existential, but the direction is dangerous, which is why a +0.35 threat reading and a mild de-escalatory stance are appropriate: the US holds leverage (existing 25% tariffs on $250B, persistent enforcement/structural demands per Kudlow) and has a viable summit off-ramp (June 18 phone call agreeing to meet), so seeking a truce and holding off on new tariffs — 'negotiate' at +0.2 — maximizes US gains without courting a self-inflicted consumer hit and market selloff that further escalation would bring.
key_factors: US economy still firm (Q1 3.1% GDP, sentiment 98.2, low CPI) but 10Y yield collapsed to 2.05% and 2Y to 1.77% — markets pricing Fed cuts on growth fear
$300B consumer-goods tranche threat = regressive tax on households, ~$831/yr, 2M jobs, retailer 'catastrophic' warnings, 600+ companies' letter
China already retaliated on $110B incl. agriculture/soybeans (farm bailout ~$16B) and signaled rare-earth / unreliable-entity-list leverage
Trump-Xi G20 Osaka meeting agreed June 18 offers genuine truce/off-ramp; analysts expect resumption of talks
US retains leverage: existing 25% tariffs on $250B plus enforcement/structural IP demands
